links.outcome: Weighted emergency sensitivity of self-triage systems and LLM configurations against physician consensus
links.effect: Weighted emergency sensitivity ranged from 51.3% (95% CI 35.5-66.3%) for gpt-4.1 to 99.9% (99.7-100.0%) for gpt-6-astra; later generations more precautionary.
links.quote: Weighted emergency sensitivity ranged from 51.3% (95% CI 35.5-66.3%) for gpt-4.1 to 99.9% (99.7-100.0%) for gpt-6-astra.

links.outcome: Emergency recognition (missed emergencies) across triage systems and model generations
links.effect: Emergency sensitivity varied from 51.3% for gpt-4.1 to 99.9% for gpt-6-astra; gpt-4.1 had highest overall agreement despite lowest emergency sensitivity.
links.quote: Weighted exact three-category agreement (accuracy) ranged from 54.4% to 68.8%; gpt-4.1 achieved the highest agreement despite the lowest emergency sensitivity.

links.outcome: Comparison of LLM configurations and regulated triage systems against physician consensus
links.effect: No system performed best across all urgency categories; accuracy ranged 54.4% to 68.8% across systems.
links.quote: No system performed best across all urgency categories.

unlisted_practices: Category-specific evaluation of self-triage rather than overall agreement alone
Benchmarking self-triage systems against physician consensus using LLM-based patient actors

screen.reason: Evaluates multiple LLM model generations and commercial self-triage engines against physician consensus using simulated patient vignettes; it does not test a specific deployment practice or safeguard.
